nodes.label: Bucket ladder for long date ranges with a 3px bar floor
nodes.rationale: "The measured defect was 81 groups and 1.07px bars" (L3327). The implemented form is MAX_BUCKETS = 31 with BUCKET_DAY_STEPS = [1, 2, 7, 14, 30], first step whose ceil(days/step) <= 31 wins, and a computed ceil(days/31) fallback (L3328). The code comment states the reason: "The previous build had no ceiling, so an 81 day range drew 81 groups and 1.07 unit bars, a grey smear" (L1727). MIN_BAR_WIDTH = 3 is a hard floor in the width expression so it holds at every range length, not just the measured one, tested across 7 ranges from 1 day to 6.5 years (L3330). Calendar-sized steps are used over an arbitrary N "because a labelled bucket boundary stays meaningful to a reader" (L3328).
nodes.norm_label: bucket ladder for long date ranges with a 3px bar floor

nodes.label: Bar density defect found only by rendering, not by DOM assertions
nodes.rationale: "a real visual defect was found by rendering the chart to static SVG and measuring it, which no unit test had caught. The motivation for this whole feature is that the OLD view 'reads raw'. A chart of hairline bars is still raw, so the feature would not have delivered." (L32)
nodes.norm_label: bar density defect found only by rendering not by dom assertions

nodes.label: Single-pass collision-avoiding axis label placement: even spread first, month starts as candidates after
nodes.rationale: "The label budget is spent badly: Jul 25, Aug 1, Aug 3 are adjacent at the right edge, and Aug 3 is simply the last day, which is not a meaningful boundary. The evenly spaced ticks are computed over the whole range and then month starts are added on top, so the two rules pile up at the end." (L37). The fix replaces the two-rule approach with one pass: candidates placed in x order, any candidate within 1 bucket of an already-placed label is skipped, MIN_LABEL_BUCKET_GAP = 2, and month starts are appended as candidates after the even spread "so they win only when they land in a gap, not by piling on top" (L3333). The last bucket keeps its label only when it is genuinely a month start via isFirstOfMonth (L3333, and the code comment "The final bucket is not a label merely because it is last: the end of a range is not a meaningful boundary").
nodes.norm_label: single pass collision avoiding axis label placement even spread first month starts as candidates after

nodes.label: Once the axis aggregates into buckets, the visually hidden table must describe the rendered buckets, not the source days
nodes.rationale: "Because the x-axis now represents BUCKETS rather than days, the accessible hidden table must reflect what is actually plotted, so a screen reader is not told about days that are no longer shown. This is a correctness requirement, not cosmetic." (L46). Implemented as one row per bucket, header is the bucket's first date, multi-day buckets announced as 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-07, values are the sums within the window, single-day buckets keep the plain ISO date so nothing regressed for short ranges (L3336). The bare "to" was left untranslated because the existing copy keys have no date-range key and locale files were not in the permitted file list, rather than fabricating a key (L3359).
nodes.norm_label: once the axis aggregates into buckets the visually hidden table must describe the rendered buckets not the source days

nodes.label: Bare onClick reference never resolves in reachesPlayAudio
nodes.rationale: "the detector's reachesPlayAudio only steps into an identifier written as name(. A JSX onClick={someFn} has no parentheses, so it is reported silent even though someFn does call playAudio. Nine of my eighteen queue entries were detector false positives, not real gaps. A cue at those call sites would double-fire, so they must be registered, not wired." (L11230) The same passage records the failure being made once: extracting openRebuildDialog/closeRebuildDialog and binding them bare re-created the blind spot and failed the contract, fixed with the () => handler() call form.
nodes.norm_label: bare onclick reference never resolves in reachesplayaudio

nodes.label: A doc comment containing a literal onClick={ example becomes a phantom detector candidate
nodes.rationale: "no comment in these files may contain the literal text onClick={ -- the detector regex scans source, not code, and a doc-comment example becomes a phantom candidate. I hit this and reworded." (L11232) This is a second blind spot of the same source-scanning detector as the bare-reference one, on the write side rather than the resolution side.
nodes.norm_label: a doc comment containing a literal onclick example becomes a phantom detector candidate

nodes.label: toast-owns-cue: a control whose handler raises a toast on every outcome is registered, not wired, and the rule conflicts with a recorded prior decision
nodes.rationale: "The 4 run controls all raise toasts, so under rule 2 they are toast-owns-cue exclusions. This is the one judgement call worth your review: brief rule 2 ('or raises a toast, LEAVE IT') directly conflicts with your 'distinct buttons each need their own cue' note. I followed rule 2, and note ToastSound.tsx:20-23 records that this codebase does accept action-cue + toast-sound pairs elsewhere. If you disagree, wiring them is 4 one-line edits." (L11240) The stated reason for not double-cuing is that adding a click cue "would put two sounds on one action" while ToastSound already plays the toast.
nodes.norm_label: toast owns cue exclusion a control whose handler raises a toast on every outcome is registered not wired and the rule conflicts with a recorded prior decision

nodes.label: A peer's git stash on a shared contract file silently reverted every chunk's work in the fan-out
nodes.rationale: "A peer's git stash wiped the shared contract file. Mid-session audioCueCoverage.test.ts became byte-identical to HEAD -- my edits and every other chunk's, plus the detector improvements. The stash list is now empty, so that content is gone. I re-applied only my 12 keys + queue. You must re-apply A1/A3's and the other groups' register entries and the new self-tests." (L11252) Append-only write scope to a shared file did not protect it, because a peer ran a whole-tree VCS operation rather than editing.
nodes.norm_label: a peer s git stash on a shared contract file silently reverted every chunk s work in the fan out

nodes.label: audioCueCoverage register keyed by file:line goes stale as soon as the file grows
nodes.rationale: "Detector keys are line-based, so adding lines invalidated every later key in the same file. I re-derived all 12 from the detector's own output. If you re-apply peers' entries, their keys are likely stale for the same reason." (L11254)
nodes.norm_label: audiocuecoverage register keyed by file line goes stale as soon as the file grows
